what: Corning makes specialty glass and ceramics. It supplies optical fibre and cable for telecom and data centres, cover glass for phones and laptops, glass substrates for displays, and ceramic filters that clean vehicle exhaust.
customers: Telecom carriers and data centre builders, phone and TV makers, carmakers and pharmaceutical companies.
money: optical fibre, cable and connectivity for carriers and data centres
glass substrates for televisions and monitors
Gorilla Glass for phones and laptops
ceramic substrates and filters for vehicle exhaust
moat: Glass and ceramic processes developed over 175 years that competitors cannot copy quickly, and designs specified into customers' products years in advance.
risks: Display glass prices fall over time and the TV market is mature
Smartphone demand is cyclical and concentrated among a few customers
Capital spending on new glass plants is heavy
Vehicle exhaust products shrink as electric cars take share
opportunities: AI data centres need enormous quantities of optical fibre, and that segment grew sharply
Its Springboard plan targets several billion dollars of added sales from existing capacity
Solar manufacturing in the US is a new market it is entering
watch: Optical Communications revenue, especially the enterprise and data centre portion.
